questions.text: नीचे दिए गए वेन आरेख का अध्ययन कर P, Q, R के लिए सही उदाहरणों वाले विकल्प का चयन कीजिए : (द्विबीजपत्री P) (भ्रूणपोषयुक्त बीज Q) (एकबीजपत्री R)
questions.text_english: Refer to the Venn diagram given below. Select the option with correct examples P, Q, and R : (Dicotyledonous P) (Endospermic seed Q) (Monocotyledonous R)
questions.solution: Option (A) is correct. Castor (Ricinus communis) is a dicotyledonous plant with endospermic seeds, so it fits in region P (dicot only). Onion is a monocotyledonous plant whose seed contains endosperm, so it fits in Q (the intersection of endospermic and monocot). Wheat is a monocotyledonous plant with endospermic seeds and belongs to region R. Option B is wrong because Castor cannot be placed in Q (the shared region) and Bean in P. Options C and D are incorrect because Gram, Barley, Rubber, and Groundnut do not correctly fit all three regions simultaneously.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प (A) सही है। अरंड द्विबीजपत्री भ्रूणपोषयुक्त बीज वाला पौधा है अतः यह P में आता है। प्याज एकबीजपत्री व भ्रूणपोषयुक्त बीज वाला पौधा है अतः Q (प्रतिच्छेदन) में आता है। गेहूँ एकबीजपत्री व भ्रूणपोषयुक्त बीज वाला पौधा है अतः R में आता है।

questions.text: एक योजनात्मक पॉलीन्यूक्लियोटाइड शृंखला में '- - - -' लाइन इसके प्रकार बंध का निरूपण दर्शाती है :
questions.text_english: The type of bond represented by the dotted line '- - - -' in a schematic polynucleotide chain is :
questions.solution: Option (C) is correct. In a polynucleotide chain, the bond between the deoxyribose (or ribose) sugar and the nitrogenous base is called the N-glycosidic linkage, and it is represented by the dotted line connecting S (sugar) to B (base) in the diagram. The phosphodiester bond connects successive sugar-phosphate units (backbone), the hydrogen bond holds the two strands of DNA together between complementary bases, and the peptide bond is found in proteins, not nucleic acids.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प (C) सही है। पॉलीन्यूक्लियोटाइड शृंखला में S (शर्करा) तथा B (नाइट्रोजनी क्षार) के बीच की बिंदीदार रेखा N-ग्लाइकोसिडिक बंध को दर्शाती है।

questions.text: दूध को दही में स्कंदित करने वाले लैक्टोबैसिलस को सामान्यतः इस वर्ग में रखते हैं :
questions.text_english: Lactobacillus that sets milk into curd is categorised as :
questions.solution: Option (D) is correct. Lactobacillus is a heterotrophic bacterium because it cannot synthesise its own food and depends on organic substrates (like lactose in milk) for nutrition. It is not a cyanobacterium (which is photosynthetic), not an archaebacterium (which lives in extreme environments), and not chemosynthetic (which uses inorganic chemical energy).
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प (D) सही है। लैक्टोबैसिलस एक विषमपोषी जीवाणु है जो अपना भोजन स्वयं नहीं बना सकता और कार्बनिक पदार्थों पर निर्भर रहता है।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित पारजीवी जंतुओं (ट्रांसजेनिक एनिमल्स) में से किसे पोलियो के टीके (वैक्सीन) की सुरक्षा परीक्षण हेतु उपयोग किया गया है ?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following transgenic animals is being used to test the safety of the polio vaccine ?
questions.solution: Option (D) is correct. Transgenic mice have been developed that express the human poliovirus receptor, making them susceptible to poliovirus infection. These mice are used to test the safety and efficacy of the polio vaccine before its use in humans. Sheep, goat, and pig are not used for this specific purpose.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प (D) सही है। ट्रांसजेनिक चूहे (माउस) का उपयोग पोलियो वैक्सीन की सुरक्षा परीक्षण के लिए किया जाता है क्योंकि इनमें मानव पोलियोवायरस ग्राही (रिसेप्टर) को व्यक्त कराया जाता है।

questions.text: "मनुष्य सहित सभी कशेरुकी जंतुओं के भ्रूण में सिर के ठीक पीछे अवशेषी गलफड़ों की शृंखला विकसित होती है, परन्तु यह केवल मछलियों (मत्स्य) में ही क्रियाशील अंग होते हैं तथा अन्य सभी कशेरुकी जन्तुओं में वे फेफड़ों द्वारा प्रतिस्थापित हो जाते हैं।" कथन को प्रस्तावित करने वाले वैज्ञानिक का नाम है :
questions.text_english: The scientist who proposed that "embryos of all vertebrates including humans develop a row of vestigial gill slits behind the head but it is a functional organ only in fish and replaced by lungs in all other vertebrates" is :
questions.solution: Option (C) is correct. Ernst Haeckel proposed the Biogenetic Law (also called the theory of recapitulation), which states that ontogeny recapitulates phylogeny. He observed that embryos of all vertebrates, including humans, develop vestigial gill slits behind the head that are functional only in fish. Darwin proposed natural selection, Lamarck proposed inheritance of acquired characters, and Mendel worked on laws of inheritance in pea plants.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प (C) सही है। अर्नेस्ट हेकल ने जैव-आनुवंशिक नियम (Biogenetic Law) प्रस्तावित किया जिसमें यह कथन भी सम्मिलित था।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा हॉर्मोन मानव अपरा (प्लैसेंटा) द्वारा स्रावित होता है जो सगर्भता (गर्भावस्था) को बनाए रखने में सहायक है ?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following hormones is secreted by the human placenta that helps in the maintenance of pregnancy ?
questions.solution: Option (B) is correct. Human Chorionic Gonadotropin (hCG) is secreted by the placenta (trophoblast cells) early in pregnancy. It maintains the corpus luteum, which continues to secrete progesterone, thus maintaining the uterine lining and the pregnancy. Relaxin is secreted by ovary/placenta near parturition to relax pelvic ligaments. Oxytocin stimulates uterine contractions during labour. Human Placental Lactogen stimulates mammary gland development but is not primarily responsible for maintaining pregnancy.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प (B) सही है। मानव जरायु गोनैडोट्रॉपिन (hCG) अपरा द्वारा स्रावित होता है जो कॉर्पस ल्यूटियम को बनाए रखता है और इस प्रकार प्रोजेस्टेरोन का स्राव जारी रखकर गर्भावस्था को बनाए रखता है।

questions.text: ऐलर्जीय अनुक्रिया के दौरान, प्रतिजन के IgE प्रतिरक्षियों में बंधन से क्या निर्मुक्त होने लगता है ?
questions.text_english: During an allergic reaction, the binding of antigen to IgE antibodies initiates release of :
questions.solution: Option (B) is correct. During an allergic reaction, allergens bind to IgE antibodies that are attached to mast cells and basophils. This cross-linking triggers degranulation, releasing histamine from these cells. Histamine causes vasodilation, increased vascular permeability, and smooth muscle contraction, leading to the classic symptoms of allergy such as sneezing, itching, and runny nose. Interferons are antiviral proteins, heparin is an anticoagulant, and acetylamine is not a relevant immune mediator.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प (B) सही है। एलर्जी में प्रतिजन IgE प्रतिरक्षियों से बंध कर मस्त कोशिकाओं से हिस्टामीन का स्राव कराता है जिससे एलर्जी के लक्षण उत्पन्न होते हैं।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित से गलत जोड़े का चयन कीजिए : मानव कैरियोटाइप — लक्षण
questions.text_english: Select the incorrect match from the following : Human Karyotype — Characters

options.A: 45 + XX — चौड़ी हथेली में अभिलाक्षणिक पाम क्रीज़
options.B: 44 + XXY — समग्र रूप से मादा लक्षण का विकास
options.C: 44 + XO — अल्पवर्धित अंडाशय के कारण नारी बाँझ होती है

options_english.A: 45 + XX — Broad palm with characteristic palm crease
options_english.C: 44 + XO — Sterile females as ovaries are rudimentary

questions.solution: Option (A) is incorrect and hence the answer. The karyotype 45 + XX (total 47 chromosomes with trisomy 21) describes Down syndrome, whose features include a broad palm with a single transverse palmar crease (simian crease). However, the total chromosome count in Down syndrome is 47 (44 autosomes + 2 sex chromosomes + 1 extra chromosome 21), written as 2n = 47. Writing it as 45+XX is the incorrect representation because 45 autosomes + XX would give 47 total, not standard notation. The correct pairing should be 44 autosomes + 2 sex chromosomes + 1 extra = trisomy. The other options B (Klinefelter: 44+XXY = overall feminine), C (Turner: 44+XO = sterile female), and D (44+XY = normal male) are all correct.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प (A) गलत है। 45+XX डाउन सिंड्रोम का सही निरूपण नहीं है। शेष सभी जोड़े सही हैं।

questions.text: प्रतिबंधन एंडोन्यूक्लिएज़ – हिंड II डीएनए अणु के विशिष्ट अनुक्रम को पहचान कर विशेष बिन्दु पर काटते हैं, इस विशिष्ट अनुक्रम में क्षारक युग्मों की संख्या है :
questions.text_english: Restriction Endonuclease Hind II always cuts DNA molecules at a particular point by recognising a specific sequence of :
questions.solution: Option (A) is correct. Hind II was the first restriction endonuclease to be discovered. It recognises a specific sequence of six base pairs in the DNA molecule and cuts it at a particular point within that sequence. It was the discovery of Hind II that led to the concept of restriction enzymes as molecular scissors in biotechnology.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प (A) सही है। हिंड II प्रतिबंधन एंडोन्यूक्लिएज़ डीएनए में छह क्षारक युग्मों के विशिष्ट अनुक्रम को पहचानकर उसे काटता है।

questions.text: परिवार नियोजन हेतु किसी दम्पति द्वारा अपनाई जाने वाली आवधिक संयम अवधि होनी चाहिए :
questions.text_english: The periodic abstinence by a couple for family planning should be from :

options.A: माहवारी चक्र के 5वें से 10वें दिन के बीच
options.B: माहवारी चक्र के 13वें से 15वें दिन के बीच
options.C: माहवारी चक्र के 10वें से 17वें दिन के बीच
options.D: माहवारी चक्र के 16वें से 20वें दिन के बीच

questions.solution: Option (C) is correct. The periodic abstinence (rhythm method or calendar method) is based on avoiding intercourse during the fertile period of the menstrual cycle. Ovulation typically occurs around day 14 of a 28-day cycle. Considering the lifespan of the ovum (1-2 days) and sperm (up to 72 hours), the fertile window is approximately from day 10 to day 17. Couples should abstain from intercourse during this period to avoid pregnancy.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प (C) सही है। माहवारी चक्र में लगभग 14वें दिन अंडोत्सर्ग होता है तथा अंडाणु और शुक्राणु की जीवित रहने की अवधि को ध्यान में रखते हुए 10वें से 17वें दिन के बीच की अवधि उर्वर होती है।

questions.text: स्टैनले कोहेन व हरबर्ट बोयर ने प्रथम r-डीएनए के निर्माण के लिए निम्नलिखित में से किस जीवाणु (बैक्टीरिया) का उपयोग किया ?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following bacteria were used by Stanley Cohen and Herbert Boyer to accomplish the construction of the first rDNA ?
questions.solution: Option (C) is correct. In 1972, Stanley Cohen and Herbert Boyer used E. coli (Escherichia coli) as the host organism to construct the first recombinant DNA molecule. They isolated a plasmid from E. coli, cut it with a restriction enzyme, inserted a foreign gene, and introduced the recombinant plasmid back into E. coli cells, where it was successfully replicated and expressed. This landmark experiment laid the foundation of recombinant DNA technology.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प (C) सही है। स्टैनले कोहेन और हरबर्ट बोयर ने ई. कोलाई जीवाणु का उपयोग करके पहला पुनर्संयोजित डीएनए (rDNA) बनाया।

questions.text: एक तालाब के पारितंत्र में एक से अधिक पोषण स्तर पर विद्यमान जीव है :
questions.text_english: The organism that occupies more than one trophic level in a pond ecosystem is :
questions.solution: Option (A) is correct. Fish in a pond ecosystem can occupy more than one trophic level because they feed on both zooplankton (acting as secondary consumer, T3) and phytoplankton (acting as primary consumer, T2), and larger fish may even feed on smaller fish (T4). Phytoplankton is always at T1 (producer). Zooplankton is primarily at T2. Frog is mostly at one trophic level (T3). Fish is the organism that characteristically occupies multiple trophic levels.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प (A) सही है। तालाब पारितंत्र में मछली एक से अधिक पोषण स्तरों पर पाई जाती है क्योंकि यह पादपप्लवक तथा प्राणिप्लवक दोनों को खाती है।

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : भारत सरकार ने जीएम अनुसंधान संबंधी कार्यों की वैधानिकता निर्धारण हेतु 'जीईएसी (GEAC)' नामक संगठन की स्थापना की है।
कारण (R) : जब आनुवंशिकतः रूपांतरित जीवों को पारितंत्र में प्रविष्ट कराया जाता है तो उन पर कोई प्रभाव नहीं पड़ता।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : Indian Government has set up an organisation known as GEAC to decide the validity of GM research.
Reason (R) : Genetic modification of organisms has no effect when such organisms are introduced in the ecosystem.
questions.instruction_line: दो कथन दिए गए हैं — अभिकथन (A) तथा कारण (R)। सही उत्तर चुनिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Two statements are given — Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Select the correct answer.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) ग़लत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) ग़लत है, परन्तु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: Option (C) is correct. The Assertion is true — the Indian Government has indeed established GEAC (Genetic Engineering Appraisal Committee) to evaluate and approve activities related to the use of GMOs and GM research for safety. However, the Reason is false — genetically modified organisms can have significant effects on the ecosystem when introduced, including potential disruption of biodiversity, gene flow to wild relatives, or ecological imbalance. GEAC was set up precisely because GM organisms can affect the ecosystem, not because they have no effect.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प (C) सही है। अभिकथन सही है — GEAC की स्थापना की गई है। परन्तु कारण गलत है — जीएम जीवों का पारितंत्र पर प्रभाव पड़ता है, इसीलिए GEAC की स्थापना की गई है।

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : जीन प्रवाह से आनुवंशिक विभिन्नता में वृद्धि होती है।
कारण (R) : किसी प्राप्तकर्ता समष्टि में नए ऐलील की यादृच्छिक प्रविष्टि तथा उनका दाता समष्टि से हटाना ऐलील की आवृत्ति को प्रभावित करता है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : Gene flow increases genetic variations.
Reason (R) : The random introduction of new alleles into a recipient population and their removal from donor population affects allele frequency.
questions.instruction_line: दो कथन दिए गए हैं — अभिकथन (A) तथा कारण (R)। सही उत्तर चुनिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Two statements are given — Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Select the correct answer.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) ग़लत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) ग़लत है, परन्तु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: Option (A) is correct. Gene flow is the transfer of alleles or genes from one population to another through migration. The Assertion is true because gene flow introduces new alleles into the recipient population, thereby increasing its genetic variation. The Reason is also true and correctly explains the Assertion — when new alleles randomly enter a recipient population and are removed from the donor population, the allele frequencies in both populations change, resulting in increased genetic variation in the recipient population.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प (A) सही है। जीन प्रवाह से प्राप्तकर्ता समष्टि में नए ऐलील आते हैं जिससे आनुवंशिक विभिन्नता बढ़ती है। कारण भी सही है और अभिकथन की सही व्याख्या करता है।

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : हमारे देश का कानून शिशु को कानूनन गोद लेने की इजाज़त देता है और यह आज भी संतानविहीन दंपति के लिए जनकता प्राप्ति का सर्वोत्तम उपाय है।
कारण (R) : भारत में अनाथ और दीन-हीन बच्चों को कानूनी रूप से गोद लेने में भावनात्मक, धार्मिक तथा सामाजिक घटक बाधक नहीं हैं।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : The laws of our country permit legal adoption and it is as yet, one of the best methods for childless couples looking for parenthood.
Reason (R) : Emotional, religious and social factors are no deterrents to the legal adoption of orphaned and destitute children in India.

This is an Inverted Pyramid of Biomass

questions.solution: In the given inverted pyramid of biomass, level 'A' (the wider upper level) represents Primary Consumers (PC) which are Zooplankton, and level 'B' (the narrower lower level) represents Primary Producers (PP) which are Phytoplankton. This is called an Inverted Pyramid of Biomass because the biomass of consumers exceeds the biomass of producers at any given time. This type of pyramid is found in an aquatic (pond) ecosystem, where the phytoplankton have a rapid turnover rate, so their standing crop biomass at any instant is less than that of the zooplankton feeding on them.

questions.text_english: Given below is an illustration of the experiment performed by Louis Pasteur. Explain the experiment and its conclusion.

key_points: Swan-neck flask experiment to disprove spontaneous generation
Broth in swan-neck flask remains sterile as microbes trapped in curved neck
When neck is broken, broth gets contaminated showing microbes come from air
Conclusion: Life comes from pre-existing life (Biogenesis)

questions.solution: Louis Pasteur performed the famous swan-neck flask experiment to disprove the theory of spontaneous generation. He boiled nutrient broth in flasks with long S-shaped (swan-neck) tubes and left them open to air. The broth in these flasks remained sterile for a long time because the curved neck trapped dust particles and microbes before they could enter the broth. However, when the curved neck was broken or tilted, allowing air along with microbes to come in direct contact with the broth, the broth became turbid (contaminated with microorganisms). Conclusion: Micro-organisms do not arise by spontaneous generation from non-living matter; they come from pre-existing microorganisms present in the air. This established the principle of Biogenesis — life arises only from pre-existing life.

questions.text_english: Identify A, B, C and D in the table given below : (Terms — Part of the plant it represents) Pericarp — 'A'; 'B' — Cotyledon in seed of grass family; Embryonal axis — 'C'; 'D' — Remains of nucellus in a seed

key_points: A = Fruit wall (wall of the fruit/ovary wall)
B = Scutellum
C = Tigellum (plumule + radicle)
D = Perisperm

questions.solution: A = Fruit wall. The pericarp is the fruit wall, i.e., the developed and matured ovary wall that encloses the seed. B = Scutellum. In the seeds of grasses (family Poaceae), the single cotyledon is modified into a shield-shaped structure called the scutellum, which absorbs nutrients from the endosperm during germination. C = Tigellum (Embryonal axis). The embryonal axis consists of the radicle (future root) at one end and the plumule (future shoot) at the other end, with the cotyledon attached at the middle node. D = Perisperm. In some seeds, the remains of the nucellus (maternal tissue surrounding the embryo sac) persist as a nutritive tissue called perisperm, for example in Black pepper and Beet.

questions.solution: Different varieties of cheese are indeed characterised by the specific microbes used in their preparation. Swiss cheese, for example, gets its characteristic large holes and nutty flavour because of the bacterium Propionibacterium shermanii, which produces carbon dioxide gas during fermentation — this CO2 gets trapped, forming the distinctive large holes. Roquefort cheese, on the other hand, is ripened using the fungus Penicillium roquefortii, which gives it a strong, sharp flavour and the characteristic blue-green veins of mould running through it. These examples clearly show that the unique characteristics of each variety of cheese arise from the specific microbe employed in its preparation.

questions.text_english: Write the basic steps followed in the Assisted Reproductive Technologies (ART) programme to help childless couples. Why is it also known as test tube baby programme ?

key_points: Ova collected from the wife/donor female and sperm from husband/donor
In vitro fertilisation (IVF) carried out in laboratory conditions
Embryo transferred into the uterus (ET - Embryo Transfer) for further development
Called test tube baby programme because fertilisation occurs outside the body in a laboratory dish (in vitro)

questions.solution: The basic steps of the ART programme (In Vitro Fertilisation and Embryo Transfer — IVF-ET) are: first, ova are collected from the wife or a donor female after hormonal stimulation; second, sperms are collected from the husband or a sperm donor; third, fertilisation is carried out in laboratory conditions in a culture medium (in vitro fertilisation); fourth, the fertilised egg (zygote) is allowed to divide to form an embryo of 8 cells; fifth, the embryo is then transferred into the uterus of the woman (embryo transfer) where it implants and develops normally. It is called the test tube baby programme because the fertilisation and initial embryonic development takes place outside the body of the mother, in a glass vessel (test tube or Petri dish) in the laboratory, even though the baby eventually develops in the mother's womb.
questions.solution_hindi: ART के मूल चरण: (1) अंडाणु संग्रह, (2) शुक्राणु संग्रह, (3) प्रयोगशाला में निषेचन (IVF), (4) भ्रूण स्थानांतरण (ET)। इसे परखनली शिशु कार्यक्रम इसलिए कहते हैं क्योंकि निषेचन माँ के शरीर के बाहर प्रयोगशाला में होता है।

sub_questions.text_english: Explain the significance of the experiment carried out by S.L. Miller. Name the scientists whose hypothesis prompted him to carry out this experiment.

key_points: Miller created conditions simulating primitive Earth atmosphere
He synthesised amino acids from inorganic molecules (CH4, NH3, H2, H2O, electric discharge)
Proved that organic molecules can form abiotically
Scientists: Oparin and Haldane (proposed chemical evolution hypothesis)

sub_questions.solution: S.L. Miller (1953) conducted an experiment to test the hypothesis of chemical evolution of life proposed by Oparin and Haldane. Miller created conditions simulating the primitive Earth atmosphere in a closed flask. He took methane (CH4), ammonia (NH3), hydrogen (H2), and water vapour (H2O) — representing the early reducing atmosphere — and subjected them to electric discharges simulating lightning. After about a week, he analysed the contents of the flask and found that amino acids (such as glycine and alanine) and other simple organic compounds had been synthesised. The significance of this experiment is that it proved for the first time that complex organic molecules necessary for life can be synthesised abiotically from simple inorganic molecules under the conditions presumed to exist on primitive Earth. The scientists whose hypothesis prompted Miller were Oparin (Russian) and Haldane (British).

sub_questions.solution: Analysis of meteorites (stones from outer space) has revealed the presence of amino acids and other organic molecules in them. This supports the Oparin-Haldane hypothesis because it shows that abiotic synthesis of organic molecules can occur in outer space under conditions different from Earth, confirming that the building blocks of life can be formed without biological processes.

key_points: Dark spots represent nucleosomes

Formed to compact and organise DNA within the nucleus

sub_questions.solution: The dark spots in the electron micrograph represent nucleosomes. Nucleosomes are the basic units of chromatin structure. They are formed when DNA (about 200 base pairs) wraps around a core of eight histone proteins (an octamer consisting of two copies each of H2A, H2B, H3, and H4). An additional histone H1 is associated with the linker DNA between nucleosomes. Nucleosomes are formed because DNA in the nucleus must be compacted significantly — the DNA of a human cell is approximately 2 metres long but must fit into a nucleus that is only a few micrometres in diameter. The nucleosome structure allows DNA to be condensed about 6-fold in the first level of packaging.

questions.text_english: In a family, the father, the daughter and the son are colour blind, whereas the mother has normal vision. Do you think the son and the daughter have inherited the disease from their father ? Work out a cross to justify your answer.

key_points: Colour blindness is X-linked recessive
Father is colour blind: X^c Y; Mother is carrier (normal): X^C X^c
Son inherits X^c from mother (not from father), father gives Y to son
Daughter inherits X^c from both parents
Son has NOT inherited colour blindness from father; Daughter has inherited from both parents

questions.solution: Colour blindness is an X-linked recessive disorder. The father is colour blind, so his genotype is X^c Y. Since the mother has normal vision but has a colour-blind son and daughter, she must be a carrier with genotype X^C X^c. The cross is: Mother (X^C X^c) × Father (X^c Y). The offspring would be X^C X^c (carrier daughter, normal vision), X^c X^c (colour-blind daughter), X^C Y (normal son), X^c Y (colour-blind son). The son (X^c Y) gets the X chromosome from his mother and the Y chromosome from his father. Therefore, the son has inherited colour blindness from his MOTHER (who is a carrier), NOT from his father. The daughter (X^c X^c) gets one X^c from her mother and one X^c from her colour-blind father, so she has inherited it from BOTH parents. Thus, the son did not inherit it from the father, but the daughter did (from both parents).

sub_questions.text_english: Explain how it is ensured that the orchid Ophrys is pollinated by a specific species of bee.

key_points: One petal of Ophrys resembles the female bee in shape, colour and markings
Male bee is attracted and attempts to 'pseudocopulate' with the flower
Pollen gets attached to the bee and is transferred to another Ophrys flower

sub_questions.solution: The orchid Ophrys employs a remarkable strategy called pseudocopulation to ensure pollination by a specific species of bee. One of the petals of the Ophrys flower has evolved to mimic the female bee of a specific species in its shape, colour, and surface texture. When the male bee is attracted to this flower thinking it is a female bee, it attempts to mate with the petal (pseudocopulation). During this process, pollen grains (pollinia) get attached to the body of the male bee. When the same bee visits another Ophrys flower and attempts pseudocopulation again, the pollen gets transferred, thus ensuring cross-pollination. Since the flower mimics only the female of one specific bee species, pollination is restricted to that species alone.

sub_questions.solution: Co-evolution refers to the process by which two or more species reciprocally affect each other's evolution, each acting as a selective pressure on the other. In the Ophrys-bee example, the flower has evolved to mimic the female bee in appearance to attract the male bee for pollination, and simultaneously the bee's mating behaviour has co-evolved with the flower's morphology. This mutual evolutionary influence between the orchid and the bee illustrates co-evolution.

questions.text_english: Explain the mode of action of contraceptive pills taken by human females. Mention the schedule to be followed for effective outcome.

key_points: Pills contain synthetic progesterone and/or estrogen
They inhibit ovulation by suppressing LH and FSH (negative feedback)
Also alter cervical mucus and uterine lining to prevent fertilisation/implantation
Schedule: taken daily for 21 days starting from Day 1-5 of menstrual cycle, followed by 7 pill-free days

questions.solution: Contraceptive pills taken by females contain synthetic hormones — progesterone alone (mini-pill) or a combination of estrogen and progesterone (combined pill). Their primary mode of action is to inhibit ovulation by suppressing the release of gonadotropins (FSH and LH) from the anterior pituitary gland through negative feedback. Without the LH surge, ovulation does not occur, so no egg is released for fertilisation. In addition, these pills alter the composition of the cervical mucus, making it thick and hostile to sperm penetration, and they modify the endometrial lining of the uterus, making it unsuitable for implantation even if fertilisation were to occur. The schedule to be followed is: the pills are taken daily for 21 days beginning within the first five days of the menstrual cycle, followed by a gap of 7 days during which menstrual bleeding occurs. This 28-day cycle is then repeated for effective contraception.

sub_questions.solution: The first transgenic cow was named Rosie. Rosie was produced in 1997 and was genetically modified to carry the human gene for alpha-lactalbumin. As a result, Rosie produced human protein-enriched milk containing 2.4 grams of the human protein alpha-lactalbumin per litre. This milk was more nutritionally balanced and suitable for human infants than normal cow's milk, making it valuable as a substitute for human breast milk, especially for neonates who cannot be breastfed.

sub_questions.solution: The naming of restriction endonucleases follows a standard convention based on the organism from which they are isolated. sub_questions.solution: The uneven distribution of species diversity across different regions of the world is referred to as the latitudinal gradient in species diversity (or simply latitudinal diversity gradient). Species richness generally increases as we move from the poles towards the tropics, with the tropics harbouring the highest biodiversity. This uneven distribution is also related to the concept of alpha, beta, and gamma diversity, where the overall diversity across different habitats is called gamma diversity.

sub_questions.text_english: Why is it that prokaryotes do not have an estimated number of their species diversity as seen in plants and animals ? Explain.

key_points: Prokaryotes lack clear morphological distinctions making species identification difficult
Most prokaryotes cannot be cultured in lab conditions
Rapid mutation rates and horizontal gene transfer make species boundaries unclear

sub_questions.solution: Prokaryotes do not have a well-estimated number of species for several reasons. First, prokaryotes have very little morphological diversity — they look alike under a microscope and cannot be reliably classified by physical appearance alone. Second, the vast majority of prokaryotes (estimated at over 99%) cannot be grown or cultured under laboratory conditions, making them impossible to identify and classify by traditional methods. Third, prokaryotes reproduce asexually and undergo rapid horizontal gene transfer, making the concept of a species (based on reproductive isolation) difficult to apply. Because of these challenges, we are unable to accurately estimate the total number of prokaryotic species, unlike plants and animals where morphological and reproductive characters provide clearer species boundaries.

sub_questions.solution: The sites in a plasmid where antibiotic resistance genes (like ampicillin and tetracycline resistance) are located are called selectable markers. In genetic engineering, selectable markers serve a crucial role: they help in distinguishing transformed bacteria (those that have taken up the recombinant plasmid) from non-transformed bacteria. When a foreign gene is inserted into one of these marker genes (say the tetracycline resistance gene), it undergoes insertional inactivation — the marker gene is disrupted and no longer functional. By plating bacteria on media containing the relevant antibiotics, scientists can identify which colonies are transformed (grow on ampicillin but not tetracycline) and which are non-recombinant transformants (grow on both antibiotics) or non-transformants (grow on neither).

A properly labelled diagram of the blastocyst should show: (1) Trophoblast — the outer layer of cells that will form the placenta and extra-embryonic membranes; (2) Inner Cell Mass (ICM) / Embryoblast — a group of cells on one side of the blastocoel that will develop into the actual embryo; (3) Blastocoel — the fluid-filled central cavity of the blastocyst. The blastocyst attaches to the uterine endometrium approximately 7 days after fertilisation, initiating implantation.

sub_questions.text: अंतरोपण के बाद भ्रूण में होने वाले परिवर्तनों का (1) अपरा के बनने तक तथा (2) तीन जनन स्तरों में विभेदित होने तक की अवस्था का वर्णन कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain the changes that the different parts of the embryo undergo after implantation up till (1) Placenta formation and (2) formation of three germ layers.

key_points: Trophoblast cells proliferate and form finger-like projections (chorionic villi) that interdigitate with uterine tissue to form placenta
Inner cell mass (embryoblast) differentiates into the three germ layers through the process of gastrulation: ectoderm, mesoderm, and endoderm

sub_questions.solution: After implantation, the trophoblast cells proliferate rapidly and differentiate into an inner layer (cytotrophoblast) and an outer syncytiotrophoblast. The trophoblast develops finger-like projections called chorionic villi, which penetrate into the uterine endometrium. These villi interdigitate with the uterine tissue and maternal blood vessels to form the placenta, which is the functional unit for exchange of nutrients, gases, and waste between mother and foetus. Simultaneously, the inner cell mass (embryoblast) undergoes gastrulation — the cells rearrange to form three primary germ layers: the outer ectoderm, the middle mesoderm, and the inner endoderm. These three layers eventually give rise to all the tissues and organs of the body.

sub_questions.text: निम्नलिखित की भूमिका का उल्लेख कीजिए : (1) अपरा (2) तीन जनन स्तर
sub_questions.text_english: Mention the role of the following : (1) Placenta (2) Three germ layers

key_points: Placenta: connects embryo to mother, exchanges nutrients/O2/CO2/waste, secretes hormones (hCG, progesterone, estrogen, hPL)
Three germ layers: ectoderm forms skin/nervous system; mesoderm forms muscles/bones/circulatory system; endoderm forms gut/glands

sub_questions.solution: The placenta serves as the structural and functional connection between the embryo and the mother's uterine wall. It facilitates the exchange of nutrients, oxygen, and waste products between the maternal and foetal blood. It also acts as an endocrine gland, secreting hormones such as human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG), progesterone, estrogen, and human placental lactogen (hPL) that are essential for maintaining pregnancy. The three germ layers give rise to all organs of the body: the ectoderm forms the skin, hair, nails, sense organs, and the nervous system; the mesoderm forms the muscles, skeleton, connective tissue, heart, blood vessels, and the urogenital system; and the endoderm forms the lining of the digestive tract, respiratory tract, liver, pancreas, and other glands.

sub_questions.text: वायोला तथा ओक्ज़ेलिस जैसे पौधे पारगणकर्ता की अनुपस्थिति के बावजूद भी बीजों की उत्पत्ति सुनिश्चित कैसे करते हैं ? संतरे के बीज को मरोड़ने पर विभिन्न आकृति तथा आकार के अनेक भ्रूण परिलक्षित होते हैं। क्यों ?
sub_questions.text_english: Why do plants like Viola and Oxalis give assured seed sets even in the absence of pollinators ? When an orange seed is squeezed, many embryos of different shapes and sizes are observed. Why ?

key_points: Viola and Oxalis produce cleistogamous flowers that never open, ensuring self-pollination and seed formation without pollinators
Orange seeds show polyembryony — multiple embryos arise from the nucellar cells (sporophytic budding) surrounding the embryo sac

sub_questions.solution: Plants like Viola and Oxalis produce two types of flowers: chasmogamous flowers (which open and may require pollinators) and cleistogamous flowers (which never open). In cleistogamous flowers, the anthers and stigma are enclosed within the closed petals, and the pollen is directly deposited on the stigma, ensuring self-pollination and seed set even in the complete absence of pollinators. In orange seeds, squeezing reveals many embryos of different shapes and sizes. This occurs due to polyembryony — a phenomenon where more than one embryo develops in a seed. In citrus (orange), the extra embryos arise from the nucellar cells (maternal sporophytic tissue surrounding the embryo sac) through a process called sporophytic budding, in addition to the normal zygotic embryo. These nucellar embryos are genetically identical to the mother plant.

sub_questions.text: आवृतबीजियों के लिए बीज बनने (निर्माण) के चार लाभों का उल्लेख कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Mention four advantages of seed formation to angiosperms.

key_points: Seeds provide nourishment to the developing embryo (stored food in endosperm/cotyledons)
Seeds enable dispersal to new habitats (dispersal of the species)
Seeds can remain dormant and germinate when conditions are favourable
Seeds protect the embryo from harsh environmental conditions

sub_questions.solution: Seed formation offers four major advantages to angiosperms: first, the seed provides stored food (in the endosperm or cotyledons) that nourishes the embryo during germination when it cannot yet photosynthesise; second, seeds facilitate dispersal of the species to new and diverse habitats through various mechanisms such as wind, water, and animals; third, seeds can remain dormant for long periods under unfavourable conditions (drought, cold) and germinate only when conditions become favourable, ensuring the survival of the species across seasons; fourth, the tough seed coat (testa) protects the delicate embryo from physical damage, desiccation, and attack by pathogens and predators.

sub_questions.text: एक आवृतबीजी के एक निषेचित भ्रूणकोष (पुटी) का चित्र बनाकर किन्हीं चार भागों के नाम लिखिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Draw a diagram of a fertilized embryo sac of an angiosperm and label any four parts.

key_points: Any four of: zygote (fertilised egg), primary endosperm nucleus/endosperm, synergids, antipodal cells, polar nuclei

sub_questions.solution: A fertilised embryo sac (female gametophyte) of an angiosperm should be drawn as an oval structure embedded in the nucellus. Any four of the following parts should be labelled: (1) Zygote — formed by fusion of egg cell and male gamete, located at the micropylar end; (2) Primary Endosperm Nucleus (PEN) — formed by fusion of secondary nucleus and second male gamete, located in the centre; (3) Synergids — two cells flanking the egg cell at the micropylar end, which guide the pollen tube; (4) Antipodal cells — three cells at the chalazal end, degenerate after fertilisation; (5) Nucellus — the nutritive tissue surrounding the embryo sac.

questions.text_english:
(a) (i) Name and explain the property present in normal cells but is lost in cancer cells.
(ii) All normal human cells have genes that may become cancerous under certain conditions. Name them and explain how.
(iii) State the role of the following techniques in detection and diagnosis of cancer :
(1) Biopsy and Histopathology
(2) Magnetic Resonance Imaging
OR
(b) Large quantities of sewage are generated every day in cities as well as in towns and are treated in Sewage Treatment Plants (STPs) to make them less polluting. Study the flow diagram and answer the questions that follow.

sub_questions.text: कोशिकाओं के उस अभिलक्षण का नाम लिखकर व्याख्या कीजिए जो प्रसामान्य कोशिकाओं में तो अभिलक्षित होता है परन्तु कैंसर कोशिकाओं में लुप्त हो जाता है।
sub_questions.text_english: Name and explain the property present in normal cells but is lost in cancer cells.

key_points: Property: Contact inhibition
Normal cells stop dividing when they touch other cells (contact inhibition)
Cancer cells lose this property and continue to divide uncontrollably forming tumours

sub_questions.solution: The property present in normal cells but lost in cancer cells is Contact Inhibition. In normal cells, when cells come in contact with neighbouring cells, a signal is generated that inhibits further cell division. This property ensures that cells divide only when needed and stop when a tissue reaches its appropriate size and density. Cancer cells lose this property of contact inhibition — they do not respond to signals from neighbouring cells and continue to proliferate uncontrollably, leading to the formation of a mass of cells called a tumour (neoplasm). This unregulated growth can invade surrounding tissues (malignant tumour) or remain localised (benign tumour).

sub_questions.text: मानव की सभी प्रसामान्य कोशिकाओं में वे जीन होते हैं जो विशिष्ट परिस्थितियों में कैंसरजनी हो सकते हैं। उनका नाम लिखिए तथा बताइए कि वे कैसे उपयुक्त रूप में व्यवहार करते हैं।
sub_questions.text_english: All normal human cells have genes that may become cancerous under certain conditions. Name them and explain how.

key_points: These genes are called Proto-oncogenes
Normally they regulate cell growth and division
When mutated or overexpressed, they become oncogenes that cause uncontrolled cell division

sub_questions.solution: These genes present in all normal human cells are called Proto-oncogenes. Under normal conditions, proto-oncogenes encode proteins that regulate cell growth, differentiation, and division in a controlled manner. However, when proto-oncogenes undergo mutation, amplification, or are placed under the control of a highly active promoter due to chromosomal translocation, they are converted into oncogenes. Oncogenes produce abnormal or excessive amounts of growth-promoting proteins, causing cells to divide uncontrollably and become cancerous. Examples of proto-oncogenes include ras, myc, and src.

sub_questions.text: कैंसर के अभिज्ञान तथा निदान में जीवूतिपरीक्षा (बायोप्सी) तथा ऊतक विकृति (हिस्टोपैथोलॉजी) की भूमिका का उल्लेख कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: State the role of Biopsy and Histopathology in detection and diagnosis of cancer.

key_points: Biopsy: removal of a piece of suspected tumour tissue for examination
Histopathology: microscopic examination of tissue sections to detect cancerous cells based on abnormal morphology

sub_questions.solution: In biopsy, a small piece of tissue is surgically removed from the suspected tumour site and subjected to histopathological examination. In histopathology, thin sections of the tissue are stained and examined under a microscope by a pathologist. Cancerous tissues show characteristic changes such as loss of normal cell architecture, abnormal cell shapes, enlarged or irregular nuclei, and increased rate of cell division. These features help in confirming whether the tumour is benign or malignant and in identifying the type of cancer.

sub_questions.text: कैंसर के अभिज्ञान तथा निदान में चुम्बकीय अनुनादी इमेजिंग (मैग्नेटिक रेज़ोनेंस इमेजिंग) की भूमिका का उल्लेख कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: State the role of Magnetic Resonance Imaging in detection and diagnosis of cancer.

key_points: MRI uses strong magnetic fields and radio waves to produce detailed images of internal organs
Helps detect tumours in soft tissues (brain, spinal cord, organs) that may not be visible in X-rays
Useful for detecting spread of cancer to nearby tissues

sub_questions.solution: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) uses powerful magnetic fields and radiofrequency pulses to generate detailed cross-sectional images of the internal organs and soft tissues of the body without using radiation. It is particularly useful for detecting tumours in the brain, spinal cord, liver, and other soft-tissue organs that may not be visible on X-rays. MRI can detect the exact size, location, and extent of the tumour and whether it has spread to surrounding tissues or organs (metastasis). It is a non-invasive technique and provides high-resolution images that aid in precise diagnosis and treatment planning for cancer.

sub_questions.text: प्राथमिक बहि:स्राव को बड़े वायुवीय टैंकों से क्यों गुज़ारा जाता है ?
sub_questions.text_english: Why is primary effluent passed into large aeration tanks ?

key_points: To allow vigorous growth of aerobic microbes (flocs) that decompose organic matter in the sewage

sub_questions.solution: The primary effluent (from which large particles have been removed by sedimentation) is passed into large aeration tanks to allow vigorous growth of aerobic microorganisms. Air is pumped into these tanks, which encourages the growth of useful aerobic bacteria and fungi that form mesh-like clumps called flocs. These microbes consume and break down the organic matter present in the effluent, significantly reducing its Biological Oxygen Demand (BOD).

sub_questions.text: निर्मित 'अवसाद' को क्या कहते हैं ? इसके महत्त्व का उल्लेख कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: What is the 'sediment' formed, referred to as ? Mention its significance.

key_points: The sediment is called Activated Sludge
A small part is used as inoculum for the aeration tank; the rest is digested by anaerobic bacteria to produce biogas

sub_questions.solution: The sediment formed in the settling tank after aeration is called Activated Sludge. Its significance is twofold: a small portion of the activated sludge is pumped back into the aeration tank as an inoculum to seed the next batch of incoming effluent with the necessary microorganisms. The major portion of the sludge is pumped into large anaerobic sludge digesters, where anaerobic bacteria digest the organic matter in the sludge and produce biogas (a mixture of methane, hydrogen sulphide, and CO2) that can be used as a source of energy.

sub_questions.text: उपचारित बहि:स्राव को प्राकृतिक जल स्रोतों में प्रवाहित करने से पूर्व निःसादन टैंक में अंतिम चरण की व्याख्या कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain the final step in the settling tank before the treated effluent is released into water bodies.

key_points: The treated effluent is passed through chlorination (disinfection with chlorine) to kill remaining pathogens before release

sub_questions.solution: The final step in the settling tank before the treated effluent is released into natural water bodies is disinfection, typically by chlorination. The treated effluent, though significantly reduced in BOD and free from most suspended solids, may still contain pathogenic microorganisms. Chlorine gas or chlorine compounds are added to the effluent to kill any remaining harmful bacteria and pathogens. Only after this disinfection step is the effluent considered safe to be released into rivers, lakes, or coastal waters without causing significant harm to aquatic ecosystems or public health.

sub_questions.text: विभिन्न जीव-जगतों के किन्हीं दो जीवों के नाम लिखिए जिनका आम तौर पर उपयोग जैव-उर्वरकों के रूप में किया जाता है। लिखिए कि इनमें से प्रत्येक जीव जैव-उर्वरक के रूप में कैसे कार्य करता है।
sub_questions.text_english: Name any two organisms commonly used as biofertilisers, belonging to different kingdoms. Write how each one acts as a biofertiliser.

key_points: Rhizobium (Bacteria kingdom): fixes atmospheric nitrogen in root nodules of leguminous plants
Anabaena/Nostoc (Cyanobacteria/Monera): free-living nitrogen fixer in paddy fields, also fixes N2 in symbiosis with Azolla fern

sub_questions.solution: Two organisms from different kingdoms used as biofertilisers are: first, Rhizobium (from the kingdom Bacteria/Prokaryotae) — this bacterium forms a symbiotic association with the roots of leguminous plants (such as pea, bean, soybean), where it lives inside root nodules and fixes atmospheric nitrogen (N2) into ammonia (NH3) using the enzyme nitrogenase. This fixed nitrogen is then available for the plant, reducing the need for chemical nitrogen fertilisers. Second, Anabaena or Nostoc (Cyanobacteria, kingdom Monera) — these are free-living or symbiotic nitrogen-fixing cyanobacteria. In rice paddy fields, Anabaena grows freely or in association with the water fern Azolla and fixes atmospheric nitrogen into the soil, naturally enriching it with nitrogen compounds and improving soil fertility.

OR
(b) A tall pea plant bearing violet flowers with unknown genotype is given. Find the genotype by working out different crosses only by selfing the plants. Write the genotypic and phenotypic ratios of each cross shown by you.

sub_questions.text: आनुवंशिकी के प्रारंभिक प्रयोगों में से एक प्रयोग द्वारा सुस्पष्ट हो गया था कि आनुवंशिक पदार्थ का स्थायी होना उसका एक महत्त्वपूर्ण अभिलक्षण है। उस वैज्ञानिक का नाम लिखिए जिनके प्रयोग द्वारा यह सिद्ध हो सका। प्रयोग का वर्णन कीजिए तथा उसके निष्कर्ष का वर्णन कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Stability, as one of the properties of genetic material, was very evident in one of the very early experiments in genetics. Name the scientist and describe his experiment. State the conclusion he arrived at.

key_points: Scientist: Frederick Griffith (1928) - Griffith's Transformation Experiment
Used two strains of Streptococcus pneumoniae: virulent smooth (S) strain and non-virulent rough (R) strain
Heat-killed S strain mixed with live R strain transformed R into virulent S type
Conclusion: A transforming principle (later identified as DNA by Avery, MacLeod, McCarty) passed from dead S to live R cells, making them virulent

sub_questions.solution: The scientist is Frederick Griffith, who performed his famous transformation experiment in 1928 to demonstrate the stability of genetic material. Griffith worked with two strains of the bacterium Streptococcus pneumoniae: the smooth (S) strain, which has a polysaccharide coat and is virulent (causes pneumonia in mice), and the rough (R) strain, which lacks the coat and is non-virulent. Griffith conducted four sets of experiments. In the first, he injected live S strain into mice — the mice died. In the second, he injected live R strain — mice survived. In the third, he injected heat-killed S strain — mice survived. In the fourth and most important experiment, he injected a mixture of heat-killed S strain with live R strain — the mice died. From the dead mice, he recovered live virulent S strain bacteria. Griffith concluded that something from the heat-killed S bacteria had transformed the live R bacteria into virulent S bacteria. He called this the transforming principle. Later in 1944, Avery, MacLeod, and McCarty demonstrated that the transforming principle was DNA. This experiment showed that DNA (the genetic material) is stable enough to survive even after the cell is killed and can be transferred to another cell where it expresses itself — demonstrating the stability of genetic material.

sub_questions.text: आपको बैंगनी फूलों वाला मटर का एक लंबा पौधा दिया गया जिसका जीनीप्ररूप (जीनोटाइप) ज्ञात नहीं है। पौधों में केवल स्वपरागण के द्वारा किए गए विभिन्न क्रॉसों की सहायता से पौधे का जीनीप्ररूप (जीनोटाइप) ज्ञात कीजिए। अपने द्वारा बनाए गए प्रत्येक क्रॉस का जीनीप्ररूपी (जीनोटाइपी) तथा दृश्यप्ररूपी (फीनोटाइपी) अनुपात लिखिए।
sub_questions.text_english: A tall pea plant bearing violet flowers with unknown genotype is given. Find the genotype by working out different crosses only by selfing the plants. Write the genotypic and phenotypic ratios of each cross shown by you.

key_points: Possible genotypes for tall-violet: TTFF, TTFf, TtFF, TtFf (T=tall dominant, F=violet dominant)
Selfing TTFF: all tall violet (1:0); Genotypic ratio 1 TTFF; Phenotypic ratio all tall violet
Selfing TtFf: 9:3:3:1 phenotypic ratio; 1:2:1:2:4:2:1:2:1 genotypic ratio
The genotype is determined by observing the offspring ratios

sub_questions.solution: Let T = tall (dominant), t = dwarf (recessive), F = violet (dominant), f = white (recessive). The plant is tall and violet, so possible genotypes are: TTFF, TTFf, TtFF, or TtFf. We selfing the plant to determine its genotype. If selfing produces all tall violet offspring in a 1:0 ratio with no segregation, the plant is homozygous dominant TTFF (Genotypic ratio: 1 TTFF; Phenotypic ratio: all tall violet 1:0:0:0). If selfing produces tall violet and tall white in a 3:1 ratio, then the plant is TTFf (Genotypic ratio: 1TTFf : 2 TTFf wait — 1TTFF : 2TTFf : 1TTff; Phenotypic ratio: 3 tall violet : 1 tall white). If selfing produces tall violet and dwarf violet in a 3:1 ratio, the plant is TtFF (Genotypic ratio: 1TTFF : 2TtFF : 1ttFF; Phenotypic ratio: 3 tall violet : 1 dwarf violet). If selfing produces tall violet : tall white : dwarf violet : dwarf white in a 9:3:3:1 ratio, the plant is TtFf (Genotypic ratio: 1TTFF : 2TTFf : 1TTff : 2TtFF : 4TtFf : 2Ttff : 1ttFF : 2ttFf : 1ttff; Phenotypic ratio: 9 tall violet : 3 tall white : 3 dwarf violet : 1 dwarf white). By observing which ratio appears in the offspring after selfing, the genotype of the original plant can be determined.
